policy.proposal_not_authority: Accepted decision rows are backed by their architecture records; every other question and every incomplete domain proposal remains review input and does not select numeric results.
policy.support_boundary: A target profile may reject an operation/type tuple, but it may not silently change the portable result of an accepted tuple.
policy.bounded_variation: A portable rule may delegate a result dimension only to a named target profile or visible numeric mode with a finite or mathematically testable allowed-result contract.
policy.cpu_boundary: CPU observations are implementation-under-test diagnostics and are never an architectural profile or independent oracle.
policy.fail_closed: Unknown identities, modes, formats, operation/type tuples, and missing delegated rules reject before architectural effects.
policy.promotion: S5-T2-A remains open until every proposal has an accepted PTO decision record and every domain has an accepted rule.

framework_acceptance.rule: PTO specifications are authoritative and backend behavior is evidence only
support restriction is distinct from result semantics
delegated numeric variation is named, visible, and bounded
unknown or missing numeric selections reject before effects
CPU observation is neither architecture nor an independent oracle

profile_proposals.role: Portable result, legality, and pre-effect rejection contract for accepted numeric operation/type tuples.
profile_proposals.selection: Applies to every PTO numeric operation; target profiles may only narrow support or implement an explicitly delegated bounded variation point.
profile_proposals.relation_to_pto_v0: Distinct from the deterministic pto-v0 raw-carrier implementation profile; it supplies the future target-conformance contract rather than changing pto-v0.

profile_proposals.role: Versioned implementation-under-test observations and developer diagnostics.
profile_proposals.selection: Cannot be selected as an architectural numeric profile or independent conformance oracle.
profile_proposals.relation_to_pto_v0: May observe pto-v0 or a CPU backend but defines neither one.

profile_proposals.role: A2A3 support restrictions and explicitly delegated bounded numeric rules.
profile_proposals.selection: Requires a complete A2A3 operation/type legality matrix and one accepted result rule for every supported tuple.
profile_proposals.relation_to_pto_v0: Future alternative target profile distinct from pto-v0; pto-v0 raw-carrier results are not inherited as hardware arithmetic.

profile_proposals.role: A5 support restrictions and explicitly delegated bounded numeric rules.
profile_proposals.selection: Requires a complete A5 operation/type legality matrix and one accepted result rule for every supported tuple.
profile_proposals.relation_to_pto_v0: Future alternative target profile distinct from pto-v0; pto-v0 raw-carrier results are not inherited as hardware arithmetic.

decision_proposals.title: profile identity and support-versus-semantics boundary
decision_proposals.proposed_rule: ADR 0041 closes the A2A3 unsupported-in-profile rule for all six MX CUBE selectors and all 25 TileDataType identities. Legal PTO operations otherwise use pto-numeric-v1 results. A2A3 and A5 may reject only documented operation/type tuples; any accepted target-dependent result must be selected by a named profile and bounded rule. CPU observations are never normative.
open_items: complete every remaining domain operation/type applicability table after the accepted A2A3 MX negative slice
accept one portable or target disposition for every supported and rejected tuple
acceptance_evidence: accepted profile taxonomy and version identifiers

decision_proposals.title: numeric format encodings and target availability
decision_proposals.proposed_rule: The 0.58.0 contract closes five distinct code namespaces and all 25 TileDataType identities, raw widths, reserved codes, and packed four-bit order. All 16 published public type identities have unambiguous catalog bindings and retain the A2/A3-versus-A5 availability baseline. Operation/type/profile legality and implementation conformance remain open. Backend carrier types cannot create implicit PTO formats.
open_items: bind the specialized floating raw carriers and decide the public roles of F64 and E8M0
publish bit-exact payload fields and exceptional-value classes for every floating type
complete scalar and tile operation/type legality matrix
resolve the E5M2/E5M3FN spelling conflict
publish positive and negative target-availability vectors for every accepted tuple

decision_proposals.title: rounding taxonomy, selection, and tie behavior
decision_proposals.proposed_rule: ADR 0047 accepts the separate scalar, fixed-mnemonic, bundle, and public selector mappings; exact RNE, RTM, RTP, RTZ, RNA, RTO, and RHB tie rules; scalar reserved-code RNE fallback; operation defaults; one rounding point for every affected domain; and rounding before saturation. Other numeric result dimensions remain owned by PD-02 and PD-05 through PD-12; PD-04 is separately accepted by ADR 0049.

decision_proposals.title: subnormal handling, FTZ, and numeric mode state
decision_proposals.proposed_rule: ADR 0049 fixes the pto-hardware-numeric-0.58.0-ieee-v1 rule: preserve every defined input subnormal, use gradual underflow for every defined result subnormal, detect tininess after rounding, expose no FTZ/DAZ architectural state or operation override, and reject a nonconforming configuration before effects. The rule is conditional on independent operation/type support and does not change pto-v0.

decision_proposals.title: NaN, infinity, signed zero, and payload rules
decision_proposals.proposed_rule: ADR 0050 accepts a bounded named-hardware checkpoint for canonical produced NaNs, NaN and signed-zero comparison results, and min/max NaN and signed-zero selection across 8 operations and 154 conditional operation/type tuples. PD-05 remains open for infinity arithmetic, broader NaN creation, conversions, reductions, quantization, matrix operations, and the complete flag/status contract.
open_items: extend bit-exact NaN creation rules beyond comparison and min/max
define infinity arithmetic and special results for conversions, reductions, quantization, and matrix operations
complete signaling-NaN flag and status interactions for every affected family
acceptance_evidence: bit-exact special-value table extending the accepted ADR 0050 checkpoint
binary, unary, conversion, compare, reduction, quantization, and matrix vectors

decision_proposals.title: scalar numeric exception flags
decision_proposals.proposed_rule: NV, DZ, OF, UF, and NX are portable sticky architectural flags with the state, lifecycle, trap envelope, and 30-form producer ownership fixed by ADR 0038. Each of the 19 profile-owned forms still requires an exact produced flag set for every supported operation/type rule.
open_items: accept exact flag conditions for all 19 profile-owned scalar forms
define tininess detection and NX coupling in every affected operation/type rule
publish independent simultaneous-flag and special-value vectors

decision_proposals.title: conversion overflow, saturation, wrap, and indefinite results
decision_proposals.proposed_rule: Every conversion cross-product has one deterministic result, an enumerated profile-specific allowed-result set, or pre-effect rejection. The public undefined-overflow wording and CPU-only saturation cannot remain architectural outcomes.
open_items: complete source/destination/rounding/saturation cross-product
resolve the public CPU-saturation versus implementation default-OFF conflict
choose overflow, NaN, and infinity results
define non-saturating narrowing, wrap behavior, and omitted-saturation defaults per profile/type pair
acceptance_evidence: minimum, maximum, one-past, NaN, and infinity vectors

decision_proposals.title: elementary-function accuracy and domain behavior
decision_proposals.proposed_rule: Each elementary function uses a versioned independent high-precision oracle plus a named per-profile ULP or relative-error bound, domain table, monotonicity rule, and special-value table. CPU host-library and hardware primitive results are observations, not the oracle.
open_items: choose oracle and version
set per-operation/type/profile error bounds
define domain boundaries and monotonic intervals

decision_proposals.title: reduction width, order, ties, and stability
decision_proposals.proposed_rule: Integer widths, overflow, comparison order, arg ties, and stable ordering are portable and exact. Floating reductions must define an exact tree per profile or a finite/testable allowed-result contract, including NaNs, signed zero, and partial merge order.
open_items: freeze accumulator widths and trees
define arg and equal-value ties
bound floating permutation sensitivity and partial merges
acceptance_evidence: widening, overflow, NaN, zero, and partial-merge vectors

decision_proposals.title: quantization and dequantization scale contract
decision_proposals.proposed_rule: Every accepted quantized format receives equations for scale, zero point, grouping, exponent selection, rounding, clamping, packing, tails, special values, and inverse dequantization. Formats without a complete rule reject in that profile.
open_items: resolve whether the affine parameter is scale or inverse-scale/pre-quant multiplier
freeze format-specific equations and stochastic-rounding state
define group axes, sizes, and tails
define sentinels, packing, round-trip tolerances, and whether SET_QUANT configuration is architectural state
acceptance_evidence: NaN, infinity, zero, max, tie, clamp, pack, and round-trip vectors

decision_proposals.title: matrix product, accumulation, bias, and MX arithmetic
decision_proposals.proposed_rule: Publish legal type tuples and, for each tuple/profile, product precision, accumulator width/order, intermediate rounding, saturation, source-accumulator and bias order, MX scale interpretation, and special-value results. Unsupported MX tuples reject before effects.
open_items: complete legal type-tuple table
freeze dot-product, HF32/TF32 selection, and accumulation arithmetic
resolve the public A5 MX E4M3-only versus implementation FP4/mixed-FP8 conflict
define MX scale layout, logical versus capacity K multiples, and non-A5 rejection
acceptance_evidence: bias, accumulate, MX scale, overflow, saturation, and exceptional-value vectors

decision_proposals.title: bounded implementation-defined numeric behavior
decision_proposals.proposed_rule: ADR 0042 inventories all 99 domain/dimension variation points and assigns their current decision owner to pto-numeric-v1. No numeric result is unbounded implementation-defined behavior. A future delegation must name a profile or visible mode, enumerate or mathematically bound allowed results, and provide discovery metadata. Generic validation rejects unknown profiles, unknown modes, and missing rules before effects.
open_items: select one admissible route for every non-portable variation point
populate a bounded allowed-result contract for every selected delegation
add unknown-profile, unknown-mode, and missing-rule rejection vectors
acceptance_evidence: allowed-result sets for every implementation-defined rule

promotion_residuals.target: accept all numeric configuration identities and selection-framework rules
populate accepted rules for every numeric domain
inventory and assign the current owner for every numeric variation point
bind every published numeric type identity and its target-availability baseline
close every unequal-width public integer TCVT result tuple
qualify an independent oracle for every conformance lane
publish normal, boundary, exceptional, and adversarial vectors for every domain
record local CPU plus independent A2A3 and A5 target results
adjudicate every differential and obtain architecture/formal review
